newsitem.title: NETHERLANDS: Dutch give emergency aid for Palestinians.
newsitem.headline: Dutch give emergency aid for Palestinians.

text.p: The Dutch government on Friday gave 500,000 guilders ($300,000) to the Dutch Red Cross for the purchase of basic medicines to help victims of the recent violence in Gaza and the West Bank, said a spokesman for the development cooperation minister.
"The Palestinian authorities called our representative in Jericho to say they really need the medicine. We also received a call from the representative of the Red Cross in Gaza," the spokesman said.
The Dutch Red Cross has been providing medicine to Palestinian hospitals since 1991 and receives an annual contribution from the European Union, this year amounting to 700,000 ecus ($875,000).
However, today's payment is the first time the Dutch government has contributed to the Dutch Red Cross's activities in Gaza and the West Bank.
"The doctors and nurses (in Palestinian areas) are working very hard. There are a lot of wounded and the money is really needed," said Hans Akerboom, spokesman for the Dutch Red Cross.
